title: Score the jointly-fitted ORN-to-PN models once against the sealed day-0 1 Hz train
status: EXECUTED 2026-09-10. PASSED: J1 at 31 of 31 pulses and J2 at a ratio of 0.096 against a limit of 0.5. The project's first passed dynamical validation, worth a V1-limited tier on the ORN-to-PN paired-pulse and 1 Hz train observables.

spent_arrays.why_it_is_spent: scored 2026-09-09, then used as half the joint fit set
opened 2026-09-10 while characterising the latency arrays, then used as the other half of the joint fit set

why_this_is_different_from_every_previou.the_fit_now_sees_the_parameter_that_matt: Every earlier candidate was fitted to a paired-pulse curve alone, which cannot constrain the resource recovery constant, so every one drove that constant to its bound and then collapsed in a sustained train. The joint fit includes a 32-pulse 1 Hz trajectory and the constant comes out at 7096 ms, interior to its box.
why_this_is_different_from_every_previou.the_fits_have_degrees_of_freedom: Thirty-six points against four parameters, thirty-two residual degrees of freedom, and goodness-of-fit p values of 0.79 and 0.77. The previous primary had zero residual degrees of freedom and no p at all.
why_this_is_different_from_every_previou.the_holdout_is_a_genuine_unseen_cohort: Fig3G has never been decoded. It is distinct from Fig3B by stored-byte digest and by animal count, 20 against 17, matching the published legends for the day-0 and day-2-to-4 cohorts.

the_cohort.cohort: wild type, 0 days post eclosion, 20 animals, 32 pulses at 1 Hz
the_cohort.published_legend: G The average eEPSC amplitude was reduced by cacRNAi for 0-day-old flies (1 Hz stimulation frequency; wt n = 20 and cacRNAi n = 19 flies).
the_cohort.everything_else_stays_sealed: Fig3G's RNAi array, Fig5B, Fig5D, Fig6D, every remaining RNAi cohort and the whole Takagi corpus.

the_developmental_caveat_declared_in_adv: The fit set is day 2 to 4 and this cohort is day 0, and the models carry no age parameter, so a failure tests a conjunction: that the model describes this synapse, and that the wild-type 1 Hz trajectory is already mature at eclosion. A failure cannot be cleanly attributed between the two. This is the same caveat the paired-pulse holdout carried, restated rather than forgotten, and it caps what a pass is worth.

observation_model.normalisation: the cohort-mean trajectory divided by its own first element, magnitudes taken because the arrays hold negative evoked currents. Identical to the fit.
observation_model.missing_data_rule: a non-finite entry excludes that animal at that pulse only, and the count is reported
observation_model.first_pulse_excluded_from_scoring: It is exactly one for the data and for every model alike under this normalisation, so it carries no information and has no standard error. A forced consequence of the normalisation rather than a choice.
observation_model.the_internal_consistency_check_this_cont: The cohort-mean first-pulse magnitude must be a plausible evoked current for this synapse, of the same sign and order as Fig3B's 50.43 pA. If it is positive, or differs by more than a factor of five, the array is not what this contract believes it is and the run must record NO VERDICT rather than a score. This check exists because the train experiment of earlier today scored latency arrays as amplitudes and no registered check could have caught it.

the_null_is_the_refuted_predecessor: ND-06 v0.1 at its registered 0.22 and 893 ms, which predicts a 1 Hz steady state of 0.904. It is a real published mechanism rather than a horizontal line, and the previous holdout's constant null produced a margin that flattered the result.

hypotheses.name: the frozen trajectory tracks an unseen cohort
hypotheses.statement: The primary frozen model's 1 Hz trajectory lies within 1.96 standard errors of the day-0 cohort mean at at least 80 percent of the 31 scorable pulses.
hypotheses.criterion: at least 0.80 of scorable pulses inside
hypotheses.why_this_threshold: It is the same threshold the joint fit's E1 screen used on the training train, fixed there before this contract existed and reused here unchanged so that the holdout is scored no more leniently than the fit.
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: If fewer than 20 of the 31 pulses are scorable, because of non-finite entries or zero standard errors, J1 is NO VERDICT.

hypotheses.name: it beats the refuted predecessor
hypotheses.statement: The primary frozen model's weighted squared error on the day-0 trajectory is at most half that of ND-06 v0.1 on the same data.
hypotheses.criterion: ratio of weighted error, model over v0.1, at most 0.5
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: If ND-06 v0.1 itself satisfies J1 on this cohort, then J1 does not discriminate and the verdict rests on J2 alone, which is recorded.

hypotheses.name: the steady state
hypotheses.statement: The day-0 steady state, the mean of the last five normalised pulses, is compared against the primary's frozen 0.6429, the secondary's 0.6497 and v0.1's 0.9037. Reported, with the cohort's own 95 percent interval.

hypotheses.name: the secondary model, and the independent check that disagrees with the selection
hypotheses.statement: The secondary model is scored on the same cohort and reported. The committed selection rule made facilitation-depression primary on a joint residual of 25.5 against 25.9, a difference of 0.4 on 32 degrees of freedom and therefore meaningless; the independent Kazama and Wilson check, which was deliberately kept out of the objective, favours the secondary decisively, 0.532 against 0.195 for a measured 0.60. If the holdout also favours the secondary, that is recorded as the fit set having been unable to choose and an independent observable having chosen for it. It does not retrospectively make the secondary the primary: the selection rule was committed and it stands.

expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.prediction: The primary is expected to pass J1 and J2. Its 1 Hz steady state of 0.643 is close to the day-2-to-4 measured 0.703, and v0.1's 0.904 is far from it, so the comparison should be decisive unless the day-0 cohort differs substantially from the day-2-to-4 one.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.what_would_be_the_informative_surprise: A day-0 steady state near 0.9. That would mean the wild-type synapse depresses much less at eclosion than at two to four days, the developmental caveat would dominate, and the holdout would have tested maturation rather than the model.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.why_this_is_written_down: So that an expected pass cannot be reported afterwards as a stronger confirmation than it is.

acceptance.verdict_rule: PASS if and only if J1 and J2 both pass. J3 and J4 are reported and do not enter the verdict.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_establish: That a short-term-plasticity model for the ORN-to-PN synapse, fitted to a paired-pulse curve and a train in one cohort and frozen with every predicted number written down beforehand, predicts an unseen cohort's train trajectory to within its measurement error and does so far better than the refuted rule it replaces. That would be this project's first passed dynamical validation, and it is worth a V1-limited tier on the ORN-to-PN train observable in one laboratory, carrying the day-0 developmental caveat.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_not_establish: Not V2. Nothing about another laboratory, glomerulus or synapse class, nothing about latencies or absolute amplitudes, nothing about any perturbation, and nothing about edge sign, which stays unresolved under ND-10. It would not resolve the release-probability incompatibility: the primary's effective first-pulse utilisation is 0.084 against a measured 0.79, and the recorded structural bound says no single-pool family can reconcile those.
acceptance.what_a_failure_would_establish: That a model fitted to both observables in one cohort still does not generalise to another cohort of the same observable, which would close the paired-pulse-plus-train route and leave only perturbation data or a different preparation.
acceptance.no_refitting: No parameter may be changed on this outcome and no successor may cite this test as evidence for its values.
acceptance.no_criterion_may_be_restated: J1's threshold, J2's margin, the normalisation, the missing-data rule, the internal consistency check and both degenerate-outcome checks are closed as of this commit.
acceptance.scored_once: Fig3G's wild-type array is opened once.

claim_boundary: One scoring pass over one sealed wild-type train array against models frozen beforehand, in a day-0 cohort whose maturity relative to the day-2-to-4 fit set is not established. It opens one array and can award at most a V1-limited tier.

execution_record.cohort: Fig3G wild type, 0 days post eclosion, 20 animals, 32 pulses at 1 Hz, never previously decoded

results.J1_prediction_inside_the_measurement_err: PASSED. 31 of 31 scorable pulses inside 1.96 standard errors, a fraction of 1.000 against the registered 0.80. The threshold was the one the joint fit's own screen used on the training train, fixed before this contract existed, so the holdout was scored no more leniently than the fit.
results.J2_beats_the_refuted_predecessor: PASSED. Weighted squared error 13.41 against ND-06 v0.1's 139.32, a ratio of 0.0962 against the registered limit of 0.5. Better by a factor of ten than the rule it replaces, on a cohort neither had seen.
results.J3_steady_state: Observed 0.5550. Primary predicted 0.6429, secondary 0.6503, ND-06 v0.1 0.9037. The day-0 cohort depresses somewhat more than the day-2-to-4 fit set's 0.7032, and both frozen models sit between the two while the refuted predecessor is far above both.
results.J4_the_two_frozen_models_are_not_separat: Primary 13.41, secondary 14.60, both inside at 31 of 31 pulses. A difference of 1.2 on 31 points separates nothing. The independent Kazama and Wilson check still favours the secondary decisively, 0.532 against 0.195 for a measured 0.60, and this holdout does not overturn or confirm that. The committed selection rule made the primary primary and it stands; neither model may be preferred on this evidence.

the_guards_that_ran_and_what_each_establ.manifest_checksum: the bytes scored are the bytes reserved
the_guards_that_ran_and_what_each_establ.duplicate_array_digest: Fig3G duplicates none of Fig3D, Fig3B or Fig3H. The guard that was missing when a bit-identical cohort was scored as a holdout earlier today.
the_guards_that_ran_and_what_each_establ.frozen_trajectory_rederivation: every predicted pulse recomputed from the frozen parameters and matched to 1e-6, so the simulator has not moved under the freeze
the_guards_that_ran_and_what_each_establ.internal_consistency_check: the cohort's mean first-pulse magnitude is 49.72 pA against the fit set's 50.43, a ratio of 0.9860. This is the check that was missing when latency arrays were scored as amplitudes this morning, and it is the first contract in this project to carry one.
the_guards_that_ran_and_what_each_establ.degeneracy_check_on_J1: ND-06 v0.1 lands inside at only 0.581 of pulses, below the 0.80 threshold, so J1 discriminates rather than passing everything. Had the null also passed, the registered fallback would have put the verdict on J2 alone.

execution_record.what_this_establishes: That a short-term-plasticity model for the ORN-to-PN synapse, fitted to a paired-pulse curve and a 1 Hz train in one cohort and frozen with every predicted number written down and checksum-pinned beforehand, predicts an unseen cohort's 32-pulse train trajectory inside its measurement error at every scorable pulse, and does so ten times better than the refuted rule it replaces. It is the project's first passed dynamical validation.

the_tier_it_earns.scope: the ORN-to-uniglomerular-PN paired-pulse and 1 Hz train observables, in one laboratory, in Drosophila melanogaster, across an unstated mixture of glomeruli labelled by GH146-QF
the_tier_it_earns.it_is_not_V2: nothing here is a circuit-level activity prediction

what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about another laboratory, another glomerulus or another synapse class. The recordings pool an unstated glomerular mixture through a driver labelling about 60 per cent of projection neurons.

Anything about trains above 1 Hz. The 7 Hz check is reported and the primary misses it badly, at 0.195 against a measured 0.60, while the secondary gives 0.532. That is a live problem for the primary and it is not resolved by this pass.
Anything about latency, jitter, absolute amplitude, miniature EPSCs or any perturbation.
Anything about edge sign, which stays unresolved under ND-10.

The release-probability incompatibility, which is untouched: the primary's effective first-pulse utilisation is 0.084 against a measured 0.79, and the recorded structural bound says no single-pool family reconciles those.
Which of the two frozen models is right. The holdout cannot separate them.

Developmental invariance. The fit set is day 2 to 4 and the holdout day 0, and the models carry no age parameter, so the pass is a conjunction of the model being right and the trajectory being mature at eclosion. The observed day-0 steady state of 0.555 against the day-2-to-4 0.703 shows the two cohorts do differ, and both frozen models sit between them, which is a weaker situation than either alone.
execution_record.the_honest_caveat_on_the_day_0_differenc: The day-0 steady state is 0.555 and the day-2-to-4 steady state, in the fit set, is 0.703. The models predict 0.643 and 0.650, between the two. So the frozen curve is not tracking a cohort identical to the one it was fitted to; it lands inside the day-0 error bars at every pulse while sitting above the day-0 mean and below the day-2-to-4 mean. That the day-0 cohort's intervals are wide enough to contain it is part of why J1 passes, and the registered degeneracy check confirms the intervals are not so wide that the refuted null also passes.
execution_record.no_refitting: No parameter changed. The frozen values stand exactly as committed at 042a225, and no successor may cite this test as evidence for its own values.

independent_audit.what_was_audited: The claim that male-cns-orn-pn-stp-v0.3 is the project's first validated dynamics module. The audit re-read the frozen contracts and both evidence artifacts, re-derived J1 and J2 from the raw arrays, recomputed them under a corrected error model, scored three baselines the contract never registered, and re-examined the independence argument. Nothing was refitted and no threshold moved.
independent_audit.the_verdict_stands_as_computed: J1 at 31 of 31 and J2 at a ratio of 0.0962 reproduce exactly from the raw arrays. The scoring code does what the contract says, the freeze predates the unsealing, and no parameter changed on the outcome. The arithmetic is not in question.

finding_1_the_criteria_do_not_separate_t.what_was_found: The training cohort's own mean trajectory -- Fig3B's normalised curve, a zero-parameter predictor with no mechanism in it, available before Fig3G was opened -- passes both registered criteria on the holdout: J1 at 29 of 31, a fraction of 0.935 against the 0.80 threshold, and J2 at a ratio of 0.2446 against the 0.5 limit. A constant fitted to the holdout itself passes at 31 of 31 and a ratio of 0.1713.

the_table.columns: weighted SSE, ratio against ND-06 v0.1, pulses inside of 31, RMSE, RMSE over observed range, RMSE over observed mean
the_table.note_on_the_noise_floor: The primary's RMSE of 0.0873 is below the mean standard error of 0.127, so the model sits inside the measurement noise. So does every predictor in the bottom three rows. Being inside the noise is what J1 tests, and at this sample size it is not discriminating.

finding_1_the_criteria_do_not_separate_t.what_it_costs_the_claim: J1 and J2 as registered establish that the frozen curve is not wrong at 1 Hz and that it beats the refuted ND-06 v0.1 decisively. They do not establish that the mechanism is identified, because a curve carrying no mechanism at all clears the same two bars. The model does beat that baseline, 13.41 against 34.08, but that margin was not a registered criterion and may not be claimed as a passed test.
finding_1_the_criteria_do_not_separate_t.what_it_does_not_cost: The degeneracy check registered in the contract was not wrong. It asked whether the refuted predecessor passes J1 and correctly found that it does not, at 0.581. What was missing is a strong baseline drawn from the training data, and no criterion in this project has ever carried one. That is the concrete design lesson and it belongs in the next contract.

finding_2_the_goodness_of_fit_p_is_inval.what_was_claimed: A chi-square goodness of fit of 25.4578 on 32 residual degrees of freedom, p = 0.7871, computed as 36 points minus 4 parameters.
finding_2_the_goodness_of_fit_p_is_inval.why_it_is_wrong: It treats 36 correlated repeated measures as 36 independent observations. The 31 train points come from repeated stimulation of the same cells; every one is divided by the same estimated first-pulse mean, which correlates all of them by construction; and the methods say several protocols were run in one cell, so the 5 paired-pulse points are probably not independent of the 31 train points either.
finding_2_the_goodness_of_fit_p_is_inval.the_corrected_statement: The effective dimensionality of the 31-pulse train block is roughly 5, not 31. Scored properly as a Mahalanobis distance on the leading principal components of the bootstrap covariance, the primary gives chi-square 2.70 on 5 degrees of freedom, p = 0.75, and 9.19 on 10, p = 0.51, while ND-06 v0.1 gives 27.77 on 5, p = 4.0e-05, and 62.93 on 10, p = 1.0e-09. So the conclusion that the model is statistically consistent with the data survives, and the rejection of the null survives strongly. What does not survive is the specific figure p = 0.79 on 32 degrees of freedom, or any claim resting on 36 independent observations. Four parameters constrained by roughly 5 to 10 effective degrees of freedom is a far weaker constraint than the artifact implies.
finding_2_the_goodness_of_fit_p_is_inval.where_the_wrong_number_appears: In this registry's primary_rule and secondary_rule as goodness_of_fit_p and degrees_of_freedom, in the joint-fit artifact, and in ADR-2026-013's eleventh amendment. The values are left in place because they are what the frozen run computed and rewriting them would falsify the record. This block is the correction and it travels with them.

finding_3_the_registered_error_bars_are_.what_was_found: The registered standard error divides each pulse's raw standard error by the point estimate of the first-pulse cohort mean, treating that denominator as exact. Because an animal with a large first response also has large later responses, the ratio is more stable than its numerator, and the correct bootstrap standard error of the normalised mean is smaller -- between 0.44 and 0.85 times the registered value across the 31 pulses. The intervals J1 used are therefore about 1.2 to 2.3 times wider than they should be, which made J1 easier than intended.
finding_3_the_registered_error_bars_are_.does_the_verdict_survive: Yes. Recomputed with the proper bootstrap standard error the primary still passes J1 at 31 of 31; the secondary drops to 30 of 31 and would also still pass. J2's ratio is barely affected because both models are weighted identically, moving from 0.0962 to 0.1013. The defect flattered the test without changing its outcome.
finding_3_the_registered_error_bars_are_.the_fix_for_the_next_contract: Score against a bootstrap standard error of the whole normalisation pipeline, resampling animals and renormalising each resample, rather than propagating no uncertainty through the denominator.

finding_4_the_independence_claim_oversta.what_the_contract_says: That the holdout is a genuine unseen cohort, distinct from Fig3B by stored-byte digest and by animal count, 20 against 17, matching the published legends for the day-0 and day-2-to-4 cohorts.
finding_4_the_independence_claim_oversta.what_the_audit_establishes: Subject identity cannot be determined from this corpus at all. The MAT files hold bare double matrices and no animal, cell or date identifier exists anywhere. The authors' own plotting script carries no age label either: the Fig3B and Fig3G sections of Figure_3.m are both titled simply 1Hz. The day-0 and day-2-to-4 assignment rests entirely on the published figure legends. The authors do use that vocabulary in their own code elsewhere, Figure_6.m titling panels day 0 and day 2-4, so the labels are theirs rather than an inference, but they are not attached to the Figure 3 arrays in the repository.
finding_4_the_independence_claim_oversta.and_this_paper_has_already_broken_legend: Fig3J, labelled the 1-day comparison, is bit-identical to Fig3D, labelled the 2-to-4-day comparison. The authors reused one wild-type reference across two age comparisons, which is why the earlier developmental holdout was voided. A legend age label is therefore demonstrably not proof of a distinct cohort in this dataset. Fig3G is byte-different from Fig3B and Fig3I, so it is not that same reuse, but the argument from legends is weaker here than it would be in a paper without that precedent.
finding_4_the_independence_claim_oversta.the_disclosure_the_contract_should_have_: Fig3H is the day-0 paired-pulse cohort with n = 20 at 10 ms, matching Fig3G's n = 20 exactly, and it was opened and scored on 2026-09-10 as the surviving arm of the voided developmental holdout, before this contract's freeze. The methods say that ten seconds of rest were afforded to the cell in between recordings, which describes several protocols run in one cell. So Fig3G's twenty cells are probably Fig3H's twenty cells. The train ARRAY had never been decoded, which is what the contract claimed and is true. The ANIMALS had been, under a different protocol, and their day-0 paired-pulse behaviour was known to the analyst before the freeze. The fit itself used only Fig3D and Fig3B and the selection rule was committed in advance, so the leak into the numbers is nil and the leak into the analyst is small but real. It was not disclosed and it should have been.

the_classification_the_audit_returns.against_the_fitting_cohorts_fig3b_and_fi: biologically independent -- PROBABLE, NOT ESTABLISHED. Supported only by published age labels plus the fact that terminal in-vivo whole-cell recording cannot revisit an animal days later, which no source in this repository states.
the_classification_the_audit_returns.against_everything_opened_before_the_fre: SAME SUBJECTS, DIFFERENT PROTOCOL is the most likely state and cannot be excluded, because of Fig3H.

finding_4_the_independence_claim_oversta.one_red_flag_checked_and_discarded: Sixty exact float values are shared between Fig3B and Fig3G, including one first-pulse magnitude identical to within 7e-15 pA. This is digitisation, not overlap: Fig3B alone holds 60 internal exact repeats among 544 entries and Fig3G 46 among 640, the same rate. The two rows carrying the shared first-pulse value differ by up to 17.7 pA and share none of their 32 pulses. Exact-value coincidence carries no identity information in this corpus, which also means the stored-byte duplicate guard is informative only for whole arrays -- which is how it is used.

finding_5_the_7hz_miss_is_a_failure_and_.the_source_exactly: Kazama and Wilson 2008, Neuron 58:401-413. A discussion-section round number with no error bar: at frequencies mimicking the basal firing rate of a typical ORN, 7 Hz, synaptic responses depress by about 40 per cent but remain relatively strong. Minimal single-axon stimulation in glomerulus VM2 at a 0.033 Hz baseline, against Rozenfeld's compound antennal-nerve stimulation at 0.2 Hz across the unstated glomerular mixture labelled by GH146-QF.
finding_5_the_7hz_miss_is_a_failure_and_.why_the_primary_predicts_0_195: Its effective first-pulse utilisation is 0.0842 and its recovery constant 7096 ms. At 7 Hz the gap is 143 ms, so exp(-143/7096) = 0.980 and only 2 per cent of the depleted resource returns between pulses against 8.4 per cent consumed. The secondary's parallel non-depleting component contributes a floor of half its facilitation regardless of depletion, which is why it reaches 0.532.
finding_5_the_7hz_miss_is_a_failure_and_.the_classification_and_why_it_is_not_sof: Both, and the second does not excuse the first. The protocols are not the same observable and 0.60 has no error bar. But this project refuted ND-06 v0.2 on precisely this number when its candidates predicted about 0.08. By the same standard, the primary's 0.195 against 0.60 is a failure of the frozen module on the only external check available, a factor of three in the same direction that killed its predecessor. That the registry keeps facilitation-depression as the named primary rule while recording this is a live inconsistency, not a resolved caveat, and it is why neither_rule_is_promoted now says so explicitly.

what_the_audit_did_not_disturb: The freeze order. The models and every predicted pulse were committed at 042a225 and the holdout opened afterwards, gated by the contract's own values_opened flag and by the fit-artifact checksum the holdout runner requires.

The five guards. Each ran and each established what it claims, including the internal consistency check on the first-pulse magnitude, which remains the first check in this project that the data could fail on their own terms.
The Stage 2 exit gate, unchanged at v4, 0 of 3, and V0 Structural as the only supported stage tier. The artifacts stated this correctly and the audit confirms it.
The single-pool release-probability bound and the ND-10 edge-sign gap, both untouched by the pass and correctly recorded as untouched.
independent_audit.the_narrowest_defensible_claim: Two ORN-to-PN short-term-plasticity models, fitted jointly to a spent paired-pulse curve and a spent 1 Hz train and frozen with every predicted value checksum-pinned before the test array was opened, reproduce an unseen day-0 wild-type 32-pulse 1 Hz trajectory within its pointwise measurement error at all 31 scorable pulses, with a weighted residual of 13.41 against the refuted ND-06 v0.1's 139.32. The registered criteria are also satisfied by the training cohort's own mean trajectory, so this is a demonstrated absence of contradiction at 1 Hz and a decisive improvement on v0.1, not an identification of the mechanism. Scoring is pointwise on correlated repeated measures worth roughly 3 to 10 independent checks. The holdout's biological independence from the fit set rests on published age labels in a paper that has already reused a wild-type array across age labels. The frozen primary misses the only external observable by a factor of three.
